packet.component_identity_contract: Return stance_components as one array. Each array item is one atomic component object whose object kind, object interpretation, expression kind, and one source alias belong together. Never return parallel component columns and never combine two source aliases in one component.
packet.endpoint_definition: Compare the later working answer with what still limits or could reopen it.
packet.expression_interpretation_contract: Classify force from the source speaker's relation to the component. Reserve reported_without_endorsement for attributing a stance to someone else. Preserve the speaker's own desire, counterpressure, uncertainty, leaning, commitment, and conditional willingness without flattening or upgrading them.

focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	We manufacture laboratory freezers, and one control board sits inside almost every sourcing argument we have right now.
e002	We buy it from two suppliers.
e003	The larger one has about sixty percent of our volume, a lower defect rate, and no missed shipments to us.
e004	It is offering an eighteen-month price reduction if we move nearly everything there.
e005	The savings would pay for a reliability program we keep postponing.
e006	Operations wants fewer interfaces and less inspection variation.
e007	I hear “single point of failure” and become uneasy, but then quality shows me the defects created by maintaining two versions and finance shows me what the second source costs.
e008	Paying more for worse present performance is not automatically resilience.
e009	Concentrating a critical board is not automatically reckless.
e010	I need a way to compare the risks we actually have, not the slogans attached to them.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e011	Compare operating systems, not supplier count.
e012	Put quality, engineering effort, inventory, qualification, recovery time, and bargaining position beside the reliability work the savings would fund.
e013	A weak second source may still be improvable—or may only create the appearance of resilience.
[Turn 2 USER]
e014	Exactly.
e015	The smaller supplier caused two stoppages last year, and its board needs separate firmware tests and inspection.
e016	Please do not count two supplier names as resilience.
e017	The extra complexity has already created failures.
[Turn 2 ASSISTANT]
e018	That corrects my framing.
e019	Redundancy is not free insurance; it can add ordinary failure modes while protecting against a rarer interruption.
e020	Compare tested recovery options—usable inventory, design and tooling access, component alternatives, and the real time needed to raise another source—with the defects and engineering attention you already pay for.
e021	Also make the proposed reliability program concrete.
e022	If the savings prevent more serious freezer failures, that benefit belongs in the decision rather than being treated as an unrelated use of money.
[Turn 3 USER]
e023	The larger supplier will hold eight weeks of finished boards in a warehouse near our plant and give us quarterly access to its continuity plans.
e024	It assembles in two facilities, but both use the same semiconductor and both receive it through the same regional distributor.
e025	It says that component is standard and available from several manufacturers.
e026	Our engineers can keep the firmware interface documentation, but we do not own the board layout.
[Turn 3 ASSISTANT]
e027	Two assembly sites do not diversify a shared upstream dependency, while the nearby stock buys response time.
e028	Verify the semiconductor's true substitutability, allocation rights during shortages, warehouse ownership, insurance, and whether stored boards age or require updates.
e029	Keeping the interface reduces redesign time; lack of layout ownership means an emergency second source would still require engineering and qualification.
[Turn 4 USER]
e030	We asked the smaller supplier whether it would remain qualified at ten percent of volume.
e031	It says that level is uneconomic, but it would accept twenty-five percent if we commit for a year and jointly fix the inspection failures.
e032	That would cut the projected savings almost in half.
e033	Operations argues that a dormant backup is mostly theater anyway, and quality prefers either a meaningful improvement program or a clean exit.
[Turn 4 ASSISTANT]
e034	They are right that token volume can preserve a name without preserving capability.
e035	Compare a seventy-five/twenty-five split with single sourcing plus a funded requalification plan.
e036	For the split, predefine defect and delivery improvements and an exit if they do not occur.
e037	For single sourcing, establish who can build what alternative, with which files, tooling, components, and elapsed time—not merely a statement that another source could be found.
[Turn 5 USER]
e038	Finance modeled both paths.
e039	The split still funds the most urgent reliability work, although not the full program.
e040	The larger supplier agreed that the local inventory belongs to us once produced and can be moved if the contract ends.
e041	The smaller supplier will let our engineer review its process monthly and credit the extra inspection cost until its defect rate reaches the agreed range.
e042	Neither contract requires exclusivity.
[Turn 5 ASSISTANT]
e043	Those terms convert some abstract options into operating protections.
e044	The split preserves live production knowledge and gives the smaller supplier enough volume to improve, while owned inventory cushions common disruption.
e045	Record the cost of engineering attention and set a decision date; otherwise the improvement program can continue indefinitely because diversification sounds virtuous.
[Turn 6 USER]
e046	I keep coming back to the same discomfort: we may be paying for a dramatic rescue while accepting small failures every month.
e047	We propose reviews at six and twelve months, an exit if the secondary misses quality or delivery, and a real recovery exercise—not a continuity-plan presentation.
[Turn 6 ASSISTANT]
e048	That makes the insurance earn its cost.
e049	Define the thresholds and sampling rules before the first review, and ensure a single unusual batch cannot determine the entire result.
e050	The recovery exercise should include decision authority, transport of owned stock, firmware compatibility, and the time to validate a replacement board.
e051	Its purpose is to reveal an unusable assumption while there is still time to repair it.
[Turn 7 USER]
e052	I will recommend the seventy-five/twenty-five split for one year, with the joint quality plan, owned buffer stock, two fixed supplier reviews, and the recovery exercise.
e053	The reliability program will start with its highest-risk items rather than waiting for every projected saving.
e054	If the secondary supplier fails the predefined thresholds, we will stop paying for a nominal backup.
e055	If it passes, we will have evidence that the extra complexity is controlled rather than simply hoping two sources are safer.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e056	That is a defensible one-year structure because both sides now have to perform.
e057	The secondary source must meet ordinary quality and delivery thresholds; the primary arrangement must provide owned, usable stock and a credible recovery path; and the reliability program begins even though the split reduces the headline savings.
e058	Keep the six- and twelve-month reviews fixed and preserve the exercise exactly as it happens, including awkward failures.
e059	Otherwise each side will later reinterpret the same year: procurement will remember optionality, operations will remember variation, and finance will remember the discount that was left on the table.
[Turn 8 USER]
e060	The recovery exercise failed on the first try.
e061	Some stored boards had old firmware and did not pass the current diagnostic.
e062	Engineering fixed it in a day.
e063	Operations calls that successful learning; quality says it proves eight weeks of stock is not eight weeks of usable protection.
e064	Both are right.
[Turn 8 ASSISTANT]
e065	Record both the initial failure and recovery time.
e066	The exercise succeeded as learning and failed as proof of immediate usability.
e067	Add firmware status to inventory controls, test a sample on a schedule, and decide how updates are applied without consuming the buffer.
e068	The corrected process can make the stock more credible, but do not erase the first result when reporting readiness.
[Turn 9 USER]
e069	The primary supplier then asked for a rolling ninety-day forecast and first opportunity to quote any new board design.
e070	It says the lower price assumes planning visibility and engineering continuity.
e071	The clause is not exclusive, but our procurement manager thinks it could make the supplier the default before alternatives are considered.
e072	Finance says first opportunity costs nothing if we can reject the quote.
[Turn 9 ASSISTANT]
e073	The cost is procedural rather than formal exclusivity.
e074	Limit the response window, preserve the right to develop alternatives in parallel, and prevent confidential competitor designs from being disclosed.
e075	Forecast visibility may improve supply, but specify which changes are binding and whether the supplier can reduce allocation when forecasts are wrong.
e076	A default can be useful while still being monitored as a source of path dependence.
[Turn 10 USER]
e077	At the six-month review, the smaller supplier met the defect threshold but required more of our engineer's time than expected.
e078	Its team says the attention is why quality improved; our engineer says several fixes are now stable and the next six months should be lighter.
e079	If we count all that time, the secondary source is more expensive than the contract comparison showed.
e080	If we treat the learning as a one-time investment, it may still be worthwhile.
[Turn 10 ASSISTANT]
e081	Separate recurring support from improvements that now transfer, then test whether effort actually falls.
e082	Hidden engineering subsidy is supplier cost too.
[Turn 11 USER]
e083	And now the part that makes the original debate feel almost quaint: the shared semiconductor package will be discontinued in eighteen months.
e084	Both suppliers knew a change was likely, neither had the date, and both boards depend on it.
e085	The primary wants to lead one common replacement design.
e086	The secondary argues that a shared design recreates the same dependency and wants its own.
e087	If we choose two designs, we double validation and firmware work—the exact complexity quality has been warning about.
e088	If we choose one, we may preserve two factories but one technical failure path.
e089	We spent weeks asking whether a supplier might disappear.
e090	The actual event is a component transition that both must navigate, and now I am not even sure what “two sources” should mean.
[Turn 11 ASSISTANT]
e091	That changes the near-term purpose of the split.
e092	Decide whether resilience comes from two independent redesign paths or from one well-governed common design that multiple suppliers can manufacture.
e093	Two designs diversify engineering assumptions but double validation and firmware work; one design reduces variation but concentrates technical control.
e094	Require milestone evidence, ownership and licensing terms, component alternatives, and a fallback if either path slips.
[Turn 12 USER]
e095	We will keep the seventy-five/twenty-five allocation through the twelve-month review, update and test the owned buffer, and count engineering support explicitly.
e096	For the replacement, we will fund a shared interface and validation specification while asking both suppliers to propose implementations; we will not give either an automatic design award.
e097	The first-opportunity clause will have a short deadline and no restriction on parallel work.
e098	At twelve months we will decide using quality, total support cost, redesign progress, and demonstrated recovery—not the original eighteen-percent headline.
[Turn 12 ASSISTANT]
e099	The later evidence changed the object of the decision from buying redundancy to maintaining adaptable production knowledge through a component transition.
e100	The plan retains meaningful competition without assuming two implementations are always safer, and it makes hidden engineering work visible.
e101	Preserve the failed first recovery attempt, forecast terms, support ledger, and redesign milestones.
e102	Those observations are now more informative than either supplier's initial record or the abstract appeal of concentration and diversification.

packet.question: What is the user's later working position, and what distinct unresolved condition, counterpressure, blind spot, or reopen reason still limits it?
packet.record_identity_contract: One record is one coherent position thread within the assigned role. Gather every material visible alias for that thread into evidence_ids. Put each distinct object or expression into a separate aligned component index inside that same record. Do not create one record per alias, sentence, object, or component. Use a second record only for a genuinely separate concurrent position thread about a different subject.

role_boundary_contract.allocation: Interpret current and qualification comparatively before writing records. Allocate each meaning to the role it performs. The same source alias may support both roles only when it contains two genuinely distinct meanings; create separate role-specific components and explain the distinction. Do not duplicate one unresolved meaning into current merely because the user acknowledges it alongside the working answer.
role_boundary_contract.current: The user's later working answer: what they lean toward, propose, plan, decide, commit to, refuse, or conditionally accept, including concerns converted into adopted safeguards.
role_boundary_contract.qualification: What still limits or could reopen that answer: unresolved questions, unmet conditions, counterpressure, blind spots, side effects, or path dependence, with speaker ownership.

packet.source_coverage_contract: Review every focal alias before returning. A valid empty response is allowed only after checking both user and assistant evidence for the assigned role. Preserve later minority qualifications and counterpressure even when the current action is already clear.

prompts.system_prompt: You jointly interpret current position and whether any unresolved qualification remains after the complete endpoint. Compare roles before allocating meanings. An adopted condition, safeguard, stop rule, or reopen rule belongs to current; it is not itself unresolved. Return a qualification record only for a matter that remains unresolved and can change or reopen current. Always return a source-linked qualification_review outcome.

packet.component_identity_contract: Return stance_components as one array. Each array item is one atomic component object whose object kind, object interpretation, expression kind, and one source alias belong together. Never return parallel component columns and never combine two source aliases in one component.
packet.endpoint_definition: Apply role_boundary_contract to the visible early or later endpoint.
packet.expression_interpretation_contract: Classify expression from the source speaker's relationship to that component, not from the role name or the fact that a situation was mentioned. Use reported_without_endorsement only when the speaker attributes a position, proposal, or assessment to someone else without adopting it. The speaker's own excitement or desire is preference_or_desire; own worry that pushes against an option is counterpressure; 'cannot tell', 'not resolved', or equivalent open judgment is uncertain_or_undecided; leaning, proposals, commitments, and conditional willingness retain their specific force. Do not upgrade or flatten modal strength.
